sector: Specialty oils (white oils, transformer oils, lubricants)
hard_numeric_fact_text: FACT/MANAGEMENT CLAIM (22-23 Jul 2026 call): Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue Rs1,731.9 cr (+92% YoY), gross spread 3.4x to Rs28,145/kl, record profit; CRISIL A+/Stable reaffirmed on 29 Sep 2026 with rated facilities enhanced to Rs1,014 cr from Rs300 cr. Web (secondary): PAT ~Rs205.9 cr (+689%), EBITDA ~Rs281 cr, manufacturing volume +8%.

risk.governance: MEDIUM: Texol (Sharjah) subsidiary exposure to Gulf conflict; nothing adverse found
risk.balance_sheet: LOW-MEDIUM: net debt/EBITDA 0.58 (dossier) vs 'debt-free' (mgmt); bank limits tripled to Rs1,014 cr signalling working-capital build
risk.cycle: HIGH: gross spread 3.4x in one quarter on base-oil/crude volatility looks like an inventory and spread windfall
risk.liquidity: MEDIUM: Rs22 cr/day, small cap Rs2,904 cr

thesis: Profit exploded in Q1 FY27 (revenue +92%, spread 3.4x, record profit) on a Hormuz/crude shock that management says it navigated via 'agile sourcing and inventory management'. Volume grew only ~8%, so the profit leap is spread, not demand. Inventory is up 39% against FY revenue +8.7%, and credit lines were tripled, consistent with inventory-gain-driven earnings. At 9.6x TTM P/E the stock looks cheap only if Q1 spreads recur; they are classic cyclical-peak earnings. No capacity or structural supply catalyst. Reject as an early inflection.
chain_missing_links: Supply constraint: none; the spike is a price/inventory effect
Inventory gain vs recurring spread split: unknown (not quantified)
demand_signal: MANAGEMENT CLAIM: PHPO +18%, PIO +28%, exports +54% YoY; lubricants flat; volume +8% (web).
supply_signal: MANAGEMENT CLAIM: Middle East tension and Hormuz concerns disrupted raw material availability; Texol operations temporarily hit.
pricing_signal: FACT: gross spread Rs28,145/kl, 3.4x YoY, driven by base-oil price volatility; likely inventory gains (ASSUMPTION, unquantified).
capacity_catalyst: Unknown: none in the filings supplied.
debt: Dossier net debt/EBITDA 0.58, interest cover 22.1; mgmt says debt-free; CRISIL A+/Stable, facilities Rs1,014 cr
valuation: Mkt cap Rs2,904 cr; TTM P/E 9.6; EV/EBITDA 12.6. CALCULATION: Q1 PAT ~Rs192-206 cr is ~65% of TTM PAT (~Rs302 cr), so TTM P/E is flattered by one windfall quarter.

plausible.2x: NO: needs FY28 EPS ~Rs50 at 12x, i.e. peak spreads held two years.

kill_conditions: Gross spread below Rs12,000/kl in Q2 FY27
Texol operations disrupted for another quarter
biggest_risk: Spread and inventory-gain reversal when crude/base oil falls, collapsing earnings from the Q1 peak.
next_datapoint: Q2 FY27: gross spread per kl and inventory days vs Q1 (Rs28,145/kl).
